• #The first-person pronoun of reported speech is not changed if the pronoun of the reporting verb is also the first person.
 
• Let's see an example-

• #The second person pronoun of the reported speech is changed according to the 'object' of the reporting verb.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• She said to me, "You are a brilliant student." (Direct Speech)
 
• She told me that I was a brilliant student. (Indirect Speech)
 
• She said to them, "You are brilliant students" (Direct speech)
 
• She told them that they are brilliant students. (Indirect speech)
 
 
 
• #The third person pronoun of the reported speech will not be changed in indirect speech.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• He said, "She will buy a pen." (Direct speech.)
 
• He said that she would buy a pen. (Indirect speech.)
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the verb 'prefer' is in the present simple tense hence, use the past simple in the indirect speech.

• For example, a disarming smile can make someone feel comfortable and open up in a conversation.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, "**Detestable**" is the opposite of "Disarming." It means deserving intense dislike, hatred, or strong aversion. When something or someone is described as detestable, it indicates that they are highly unpleasant, offensive, or repugnant.
 
 
• For instance, actions or behaviors that are considered morally repulsive or abhorrent can be described as detestable.
 
 
 
• Now, let's examine the other options:
 
• **Charming**: This option does not represent the opposite meaning of "Disarming" but rather a related concept. "Charming" refers to something or someone who has an attractive, pleasing, or charismatic quality. While charm can contribute to disarming someone, it is not the opposite of disarming.
 
• **Silk**: This option does not convey the opposite meaning of "Disarming." "Silk" refers to a type of fabric known for its softness and smoothness. It does not carry an opposite meaning in relation to "Disarming."
 
• **Convincing**: This option does not represent the opposite meaning of "Disarming" either. "Convincing" refers to something that is persuasive, compelling, or capable of causing someone to believe or be persuaded. It does not carry an opposite meaning to the concept of disarming.
 
• To summarize, the correct opposite for "**Disarming**" is "**Detestable**," as it denotes intense dislike or hatred. The other options, "**Charming**," "**Silk**," and "**Convincing**," do not represent the opposite meaning of "Disarming" but rather carry different meanings or related concepts.

Now, Remaining sticks = 40 - x

⇒ 150 = {sum of length of (40 - x) sticks} /(40 - x)

Given,

Speed = 1600 m/s

time = 4s 

Distance = Speed × Time

 = 1600 × 4 = 6400 m.
